title: Knowledge check: Vue Installation and Environment Setup

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Vue Installation and Environment Setup”?
options: Use Vue CLI as the primary new-project scaffolder without checking its status.
Edit generated dist assets as the source of truth.
Expose private credentials in client-side environment variables.
Use create-vue with Vite for new Vue projects, understand the SFC/entry-point roles, and test production builds separately from the dev server.
questions.answer_key: Use create-vue with Vite for new Vue projects, understand the SFC/entry-point roles, and test production builds separately from the dev server.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Vue Installation and Environment Setup directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Installing Node.js and a package manager”, which practice is most reliable?
options: Vue is a database engine for storing server records.
Vue replaces HTML and CSS with a single language.
Vue uses declarative templates and reactive state to keep an interface in sync with application data.
Vue requires manual DOM mutation for every state change.
questions.answer_key: Vue uses declarative templates and reactive state to keep an interface in sync with application data.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Installing Node.js and a package manager”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Vue Installation and Environment Setup” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.
